Router → separate pipelines (as in the WB chatbot) | A cheap classifier picks filter / analyze / explain / clarify, then a dedicated chain runs | More predictable, but more code and an extra LLM call per message | | **B. One tool-calling agent (proposed)** | One agent with **data tools** (read) and **view tools** (change the canvas). The model decides: "girls in Ghana" → `apply_filters`; "compare…" → data tools → answer | Less code, naturally handles mixed requests ("show Ghana and compare it to Kenya"), still bounded by the tool budget | **[DECIDE]** Proposal: **B**, with a deterministic pre-check (§5) handling empty, overly long and obviously off-topic input before any LLM call. ### 2.2 The loop ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor U as User participant API as /api/chat (Django, SSE) participant G as Input guard participant A as Agent (LiteLLM) participant T as Tools participant V as Verifier U->>API: message + view state {outcome, filters, snapshot} API->>G: length, rate limit, injection patterns G-->>API: ok API->>A: system prompt + view state + history (last 6 turns) + tool schemas loop max 6 tool calls A->>T: tool call (JSON args) T->>T: validate args (pydantic + allowlists) T-->>A: rows + claim_ids (or structured error) API-->>U: SSE status: "Querying electricity results for AFW…" end A->>API: final_answer(card, narrative with tags, chart refs, follow-ups) API->>V: verify every claim tag + scan for untagged numbers alt any claim fails V->>A: repair once: "claims c_9f2 and c_771 don't match the source, please fix" A->>API: revised final_answer end API-->>U: SSE: ui_actions, answer (HTML with ✓/⚠), done ``` **Response contract.** The agent must finish by calling `final_answer`, so every response has the same structure: ```json { "mode": "filters | answer | explain | clarify | out_of_scope", "headline": {"label": "People provided with electricity, AFW (FY25)", "value_html": "12.1M"}, "narrative_md": "Western & Central Africa has reached 12.1M people …", "charts": [{"type": "bar", "from_result": "r2", "x": "area", "y": ["achieved", "expected"]}], "follow_ups": ["Which countries drive the gap in AFW?", "Show this for women only"], "sources": ["r1", "r2"], "clarify_options": [] } ``` - Tools All tools are **read-only**, **typed** (pydantic schemas, exported as JSON Schema for function calling) and **allowlisted** (indicator codes, area codes, dimension values are validated against the database before any query runs). Every data row returned carries a `claim_id`. Every tool result gets a `result_id` (`r1`, `r2`, …) for charts and sources. ### 3.1 Discovery tools | Tool | Arguments | Returns | Example use | |---|---|---|---| | `search_indicators` | `query`, `outcome_area?`, `type? (results/context/vision)` | matching indicators: code, name, unit, outcome area, available dimensions | "digital access" → `CSC_RES_BRO_INTE`, `CSC_RES_DIG_ENA_SERV`, `IT_NET_USER_ZS` | | `find_areas` | `query` (free text, e.g. "western africa", "fragile states", "Ghana") | resolved codes: `{type: REGION, code: AFW}`, `{type: COUNTRY, code: GH}`, `{type: FCS}` | entity resolution with fuzzy matching on names and aliases | | `get_definition` | `ind_code` | definition, unit, notes, source (metadata) | "what does 'expected' mean?" | ### 3.2 Data tools | Tool | Arguments | Returns | |---|---|---| | `get_results` | `ind_code`, `areas[]`, `org=WBG`, `sex/age/disability=_T`, `snapshot=FY25` | achieved, expected, **delivery ratio (computed in code)**, unit, snapshot date, per area | | `rank_areas` | `ind_code`, `area_type (REGION/COUNTRY)`, `metric (achieved/expected/ratio/gap)`, `order`, `top_n≤15`, dims | ranked rows + rank | | `outcome_overview` | `outcome_area? (or all)`, `areas[]=[ACW]`, `snapshot` | all Results indicators in scope with achieved/expected/ratio, for "biggest gaps" or "top lagging" | | `compare_snapshots` | `ind_code`, `area`, `snapshots[]` | values per FY + **change computed in code** (absolute and %) | | `get_context_series` | `ind_code`, `areas[]`, `year_from?`, `year_to?` | Client Context / Vision time series + latest value + change | | `get_wdi_context` | `indicator ∈ {population, gdp_per_capita, poverty_300, electricity_access, internet_users}`, `areas[]`, `year?` | Data360 values (from the pipeline cache), with source | ### 3.3 View tools (change the canvas; no data returned) | Tool | Arguments | Effect | |---|---|---| | `apply_filters` | any of `region, country, income, group, org, sex, age, disability, snapshot` (validated) | updates filter state; the canvas re-renders through HTMX | | `navigate_outcome` | `outcome_slug`, `filters?` | from the Outcomes page: open the Explorer with filters already set | | `highlight_tiles` | `outcome_slugs[]` | highlight tiles named in a cross-area answer | ### 3.4 Final tool `final_answer`: the response contract above (§2.2). Ends the loop. **Why typed tools instead of free Text-to-SQL:** the indicator database is small and well structured, so ~10 tools cover every question type in the brief. Typed tools give (1) no SQL injection or runaway queries, (2) correct handling of Scorecard pitfalls (disaggregation totals `_T`, sub-indicators, unit multipliers, snapshot dates) done once in code instead of rediscovered by the LLM every time, (3) computed ratios and changes that are verifiable, and (4) clear, testable error messages. **[DECIDE]** Add a guarded `run_sql` fallback (read-only connection, `SELECT` only, row limit) for questions the tools don't cover? *Proposal: no for the MVP. It weakens the guarantees and the tools cover the brief's examples.* ### 3.5 Tool errors are messages, not crashes ```json {"error": "unknown_area", "message": "No area matches 'Westeros'.", "hint": "Use find_areas first. Valid region codes: AFE, AFW, EAP, ECA, LCR, MENAAP, SAR"} ``` The model sees the error and can recover (call `find_areas`, then retry). Errors count toward the tool budget. --- ## 4. Verification: Proof-Carrying Numbers (adapted from World Bank DECDG) ```mermaid flowchart LR R[Tool row] -->|claim_id = hash of source, ind, area, org, dims, snapshot, field| REG[(Claim registry
per conversation)] A[final_answer text] --> P[Parse claim tags] P --> C{Compare shown value
vs source value} REG --> C C -->|match| OK[✓ verified badge + tooltip] C -->|mismatch / unknown id| BAD[⚠ unverified] A --> S[Scan untagged numbers] --> BAD ``` 1. **Stamping.** Each value a tool returns is registered as `claim_id → {value, unit, multiplier, indicator, area, snapshot, source}`. Derived values (ratios, changes, ranks) are computed in Python and stamped too, so the LLM never does arithmetic. 2. **Tagging rule (system prompt).** *"Every number taken from data must be wrapped as `shown value`. Never invent an id. If you have no id for a number, don't state it."* 3. **Checking.** Parse the shown value (`214.5M`, `37%`, `1,204`, `2.1 billion`) and compare it with the source, allowing for the precision shown (`214.5M` passes against `214,500,858`; `215M` passes; `250M` fails). 4. **Untagged-number scan.** Numbers outside claim tags are flagged ⚠, except years, ranks ("top 3") and FY labels. 5. **Repair.** If any claim fails, one repair turn lists the failures; anything that still fails shows ⚠. 6. **Rendering.** Claim tags become `12.1M ✓`; everything else is escaped (Django autoescape; only the claim span is allowed). **Metrics (also used in the model evaluation):** verified rate = verified ÷ tagged, and count of untagged numbers. --- ## 5. Guardrails and security | Layer | Control | |---|---| | Input | Max 500 chars; rate limit per session/IP (e.g. 20 messages / 5 min); regex pre-check for prompt-injection phrases; off-topic short-circuit | | Prompt | Grounding rules: use only tool results, no outside knowledge for numbers, units + snapshot always stated, no "high/low" judgements without a compared value, say plainly when data is missing; tool results treated as **data, not instructions** | | Tools | Pydantic validation; allowlists for codes; parameterised queries; read-only DuckDB connection; row limits | | Output | PCN verification; autoescaped HTML; charts built server-side from stored rows | | Secrets | `LLM_API_KEY` etc. only in `.env`; never sent to the browser; Scorecard key read from the public site bundle by the pipeline only | | Errors | Generic message to the user, details in server logs; LLM/provider errors and content-policy blocks caught and shown politely | | Django | CSRF on POST, `SecurityMiddleware`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `DEBUG=False` option | --- ## 6. Other LLM uses | Feature | How | LLM calls | |---|---|---| | **"What this shows"** (view synthesis) | Server pre-loads the current view's rows (already stamped) into the prompt; no tools needed; same `final_answer` contract with `mode="answer"`; cached per (outcome, filters, snapshot) | 1 | | **Ask from Outcomes page** | Same agent; it has `navigate_outcome` and `highlight_tiles` available on that page | 1–4 | | **Follow-up chips** | Part of `final_answer` (no extra call) | 0 | --- ## 7. Model configuration (plug-and-play) All calls go through **LiteLLM**, so reviewers can use any provider by editing `.env`: ```dotenv LLM_MODEL=anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5 # any LiteLLM id, e.g. openai/gpt-…, gemini/…, groq/…, ollama/… LLM_API_KEY=sk-... LLM_API_BASE= # optional custom / OpenAI-compatible endpoint LLM_FAST_MODEL= # optional cheaper model for "What this shows" ``` - **Requirements for a model:** reliable parallel tool calling, JSON-schema adherence, and following the claim-tagging rule. - **Model choice is decided by evaluation, not assumption** (§8). The README will document the results and the reasoning (accuracy on structured data, latency, cost per question, guardrail compliance). - **[DECIDE]** Which provider/key will we test with? It affects which candidates we can benchmark. --- ## 8. Evaluation (for the model choice) - **Golden set:** ~15 questions with known answers computed directly from DuckDB. They cover filters ("girls in Ghana"), single facts, comparisons, rankings, snapshot change, definitions, a no-data case and 2 out-of-scope prompts, including the brief's three example questions. - **Per model:** correct mode/tools · answer correctness (numbers match) · **PCN verified rate** · untagged numbers · correct refusals · median latency · tokens → cost per question. - `python manage.py run_evals --models a,b,c` → results table in the README. --- ## 9. Django layout ``` q1_prototype/ manage.py scorecard_explorer/ settings.py (reads .env), urls.py explorer/ views.py Outcomes page, Explorer page, HTMX partials (charts, chips, cards) queries.py typed read-only DuckDB query service (used by views AND tools) templates/ static/ HTMX + Plotly.js, one CSS theme assistant/ agent.py loop: LiteLLM tool calling, budgets, repair, SSE events tools.py tool schemas (pydantic) + implementations → queries.py prompts.py system prompt, grounding + claim rules pcn.py claim registry, parser, verifier, renderer guards.py input checks, rate limit evals/ golden questions + runner (management command) pipeline/ shared with Q3: fetch_scorecard.py, fetch_data360.py, clean.py, build_db.py data/ raw/ (API extracts) + scorecard.duckdb ``` **Streaming:** `/api/chat` returns a Django `StreamingHttpResponse` (`text/event-stream`) with events `status` → `ui_action` → `answer` → `done`. The browser uses a small `fetch` stream reader. Conversation history and the claim registry are kept in the Django session (server-side), keyed per Explorer tab. --- ## 10. Open decisions 1. One agent with view tools (B) vs router + pipelines (A) → *proposal: B* 2. Guarded `run_sql` fallback → *proposal: not in the MVP* 3. LLM provider/key for testing and evaluation 4. content.text:
I drafted `docs/platform_architecture.md`, focused on how the LLM responds. Here's the core of it.

**One agent, with a fixed set of tools.** I'd use a single tool-calling agent rather than a separate step that first classifies the question. That agent decides on its own whether a message means "change the view", "analyse the data", "explain a term", "ask the user to clarify" or "decline". This is simpler, and it handles mixed requests like "show Ghana and compare it to Kenya".

**The loop for each message:**
1. **Input check:** length, rate limit and prompt-injection patterns are checked before the LLM sees the message.
2. **Agent:** gets the system prompt, the current view (outcome area, filters, fiscal year), the last 6 turns and the tool definitions.
3. **Tool calls (up to 6):** every argument is checked against allowed values, and every data row comes back with a `claim_id`.
4. **`final_answer`:** a required structured ending with a headline number, the narrative with claim tags, chart references, follow-ups and sources.
5. **Verifier:** checks every tagged number against the source data and flags untagged numbers. If anything fails, the agent gets one chance to repair it.
6. **Streamed to the browser:** status updates first, then view changes, then the answer with ✓/⚠ badges.

**Tools (all read-only and typed):**

| Kind | Tools |
|---|---|
| Discovery | `search_indicators`, `find_areas` ("western africa" → AFW, "fragile states" → FCS), `get_definition` |
| Data | `get_results`, `rank_areas`, `outcome_overview`, `compare_snapshots`, `get_context_series`, `get_wdi_context` (Data360) |
| View | `apply_filters`, `navigate_outcome`, `highlight_tiles` |
| End | `final_answer` |

**Rules that keep the LLM's numbers honest:**
- The LLM never writes SQL. Ten typed tools cover every question type in the brief, and the Scorecard's quirks (totals, sub-indicators, unit scaling) are handled once in code.
- The LLM never does arithmetic. Ratios and year-to-year changes are computed in Python and get their own `claim_id`, so they can be checked too.
- Charts point to stored tool results rather than containing numbers. The server builds each chart from those rows, so a chart can't show a wrong number.
- Tool errors come back to the LLM as messages with hints ("unknown area, try `find_areas`"), so it can correct itself instead of failing.

The file also covers guardrails, the `.env` settings that let reviewers plug in any LLM provider (via LiteLLM), a set of about 15 test questions for choosing the model (scored on correctness, share of numbers verified, latency and cost), and the Django folder layout.

**Four decisions for you:**
1. **One agent, or a classifier step first?** I'd go with the single agent.
2. **Add a read-only SQL fallback for questions the tools can't answer?** I'd say no for the first version, because it weakens the guarantee that every number traces to a fixed query.
3. **Which LLM provider and key will we test with?** The `.env` example currently shows a Claude model only as a placeholder. The real default will come from the test results.
4. **Are 6 tool calls per message and 6 turns of history the right limits?**

Once you've settled these, I'll start building the shared data pipeline.

1 # Scorecard Explorer: Platform Architecture (DRAFT v0.1) 2 3 > Companion to `docs/platform_design.md`. The focus is **how the LLM responds**: the agent loop, tools, verification and guardrails. 4 > Decisions to make are marked **[DECIDE]**. 5 6 --- 7 8 ## 1. System overview 9 10 ```mermaid 11 flowchart LR 12 subgraph Ingest["pipeline/ (shared with Q3, runs offline)"] 13 SC[Scorecard API
ext.api.worldbank.org] --> P[fetch → parse → clean → tidy] 14 D360[Data360 API
allowlisted WDI] --> P 15 P --> DB[(DuckDB
scorecard.duckdb)] 16 end 17 subgraph App["Django app (q1_prototype/)"] 18 V[Views + templates
Outcomes · Explorer] --> Q[Query service
typed, read-only] 19 CH[/api/chat SSE/] --> AG[Analyst agent] 20 AG -->|tool calls| T[Tool registry] 21 T --> Q 22 AG --> VER[Verifier
Proof-Carrying Numbers] 23 Q --> DB 24 end 25 AG <-->|LiteLLM| LLM[(Any LLM provider
from .env)] 26 B[Browser
HTMX + Plotly.js] <--> V 27 B <-->|SSE events| CH 28 ``` 29 30 - **Data is never fetched live while a user waits.** The pipeline builds `scorecard.duckdb` ahead of time; the app only reads it. Responses are fast and the app has no dependency on the upstream APIs at runtime. 31 - **The LLM never touches the database directly.** It can only call typed tools. Each tool runs a fixed, parameterised query with arguments checked against allowlists. 32 33 --- 34 35 ## 2. How a message is answered: the agent loop 36 37 ### 2.1 Design choice: one agent with two kinds of tools 38 39 | Option | How it works | Trade-off | 40 |---|---|---| 41 | A. Router → separate pipelines (as in the WB chatbot) | A cheap classifier picks filter / analyze / explain / clarify, then a dedicated chain runs | More predictable, but more code and an extra LLM call per message | 42 43 44 | **B. One tool-calling agent (proposed)** | One agent with **data tools** (read) and **view tools** (change the canvas). The model decides: "girls in Ghana" → `apply_filters`; "compare…" → data tools → answer | Less code, naturally handles mixed requests ("show Ghana and compare it to Kenya"), still bounded by the tool budget | 45 46 **[DECIDE]** Proposal: **A**, with a deterministic pre-check (§5) handling empty, overly long and obviously off-topic input before any LLM call. 47 48 ### 2.2 The loop 49 50 ```mermaid 51 sequenceDiagram 52 actor U as User 53 participant API as /api/chat (Django, SSE) 54 participant G as Input guard 55 participant A as Agent (LiteLLM) 56 participant T as Tools 57 participant V as Verifier 58 U->>API: message + view state {outcome, filters, snapshot} 59 API->>G: length, rate limit, injection patterns 60 G-->>API: ok 61 API->>A: system prompt + view state + history (last 6 turns) + tool schemas 62 loop max 6 tool calls 63 A->>T: tool call (JSON args) 64 T->>T: validate args (pydantic + allowlists) 65 T-->>A: rows + claim_ids (or structured error) 66 API-->>U: SSE status: "Querying electricity results for AFW…" 67 end 68 A->>API: final_answer(card, narrative with tags, chart refs, follow-ups) 69 API->>V: verify every claim tag + scan for untagged numbers 70 alt any claim fails 71 V->>A: repair once: "claims c_9f2 and c_771 don't match the source, please fix" 72 A->>API: revised final_answer 73 end 74 API-->>U: SSE: ui_actions, answer (HTML with ✓/⚠), done 75 ``` 76 77 **Response contract.** The agent must finish by calling `final_answer`, so every response has the same structure: 78 79 ```json 80 { 81 "mode": "filters | answer | explain | clarify | out_of_scope", 82 "headline": {"label": "People provided with electricity, AFW (FY25)", 83 "value_html": "12.1M"}, 84 "narrative_md": "Western & Central Africa has reached 12.1M people …", 85 "charts": [{"type": "bar", "from_result": "r2", "x": "area", "y": ["achieved", "expected"]}], 86 "follow_ups": ["Which countries drive the gap in AFW?", "Show this for women only"], 87 "sources": ["r1", "r2"], 88 "clarify_options": [] 89 } 90 ``` 91 92 - **Charts reference tool results (`from_result`), not numbers.** The server builds the Plotly spec from the stored rows, so the LLM can't put a wrong number into a chart. 93 - **View actions** (`apply_filters`, `highlight_tiles`) are tool calls during the loop, so a filter-only request costs one round-trip: `apply_filters` → `final_answer(mode="filters", narrative="Showing Ghana, women…")`. 94 95 ### 2.3 Budgets and settings 96 | Setting | Value | Why | 97 |---|---|---| 98 | Max tool calls per message | 6 | Covers multi-step comparisons while keeping cost and latency bounded | 99 | Temperature | 0 | Reproducible; analysis, not creative writing | 100 | History sent | last 6 turns + current view state | Follow-ups ("and for youth?") work without long contexts | 101 | Timeout | 30 s total, 10 s per LLM call | Generic error with a retry button after that | 102 | Repair attempts | 1 | One chance to fix failed claims; then show ⚠ honestly | 103 104 --- 105 106 ## 3. Tools 107 108 All tools are **read-only**, **typed** (pydantic schemas, exported as JSON Schema for function calling) and **allowlisted** 109 (indicator codes, area codes, dimension values are validated against the database before any query runs). 110 Every data row returned carries a `claim_id`. Every tool result gets a `result_id` (`r1`, `r2`, …) for charts and sources. 111 112 ### 3.1 Discovery tools 113 | Tool | Arguments | Returns | Example use | 114 |---|---|---|---| 115 | `search_indicators` | `query`, `outcome_area?`, `type? (results/context/vision)` | matching indicators: code, name, unit, outcome area, available dimensions | "digital access" → `CSC_RES_BRO_INTE`, `CSC_RES_DIG_ENA_SERV`, `IT_NET_USER_ZS` | 116 | `find_areas` | `query` (free text, e.g. "western africa", "fragile states", "Ghana") | resolved codes: `{type: REGION, code: AFW}`, `{type: COUNTRY, code: GH}`, `{type: FCS}` | entity resolution with fuzzy matching on names and aliases | 117 | `get_definition` | `ind_code` | definition, unit, notes, source (metadata) | "what does 'expected' mean?" | 118 119 ### 3.2 Data tools 120 | Tool | Arguments | Returns | 121 |---|---|---| 122 | `get_results` | `ind_code`, `areas[]`, `org=WBG`, `sex/age/disability=_T`, `snapshot=FY25` | achieved, expected, **delivery ratio (computed in code)**, unit, snapshot date, per area | 123 | `rank_areas` | `ind_code`, `area_type (REGION/COUNTRY)`, `metric (achieved/expected/ratio/gap)`, `order`, `top_n≤15`, dims | ranked rows + rank | 124 | `outcome_overview` | `outcome_area? (or all)`, `areas[]=[ACW]`, `snapshot` | all Results indicators in scope with achieved/expected/ratio, for "biggest gaps" or "top lagging" | 125 | `compare_snapshots` | `ind_code`, `area`, `snapshots[]` | values per FY + **change computed in code** (absolute and %) | 126 | `get_context_series` | `ind_code`, `areas[]`, `year_from?`, `year_to?` | Client Context / Vision time series + latest value + change | 127 | `get_wdi_context` | `indicator ∈ {population, gdp_per_capita, poverty_300, electricity_access, internet_users}`, `areas[]`, `year?` | Data360 values (from the pipeline cache), with source | 128 129 ### 3.3 View tools (change the canvas; no data returned) 130 | Tool | Arguments | Effect | 131 |---|---|---| 132 | `apply_filters` | any of `region, country, income, group, org, sex, age, disability, snapshot` (validated) | updates filter state; the canvas re-renders through HTMX | 133 | `navigate_outcome` | `outcome_slug`, `filters?` | from the Outcomes page: open the Explorer with filters already set | 134 | `highlight_tiles` | `outcome_slugs[]` | highlight tiles named in a cross-area answer | 135 136 ### 3.4 Final tool 137 `final_answer`: the response contract above (§2.2). Ends the loop. 138 139 **Why typed tools instead of free Text-to-SQL:** 140 the indicator database is small and well structured, so ~10 tools cover every question type in the brief. Typed tools give 141 (1) no SQL injection or runaway queries, (2) correct handling of Scorecard pitfalls (disaggregation totals `_T`, 142 sub-indicators, unit multipliers, snapshot dates) done once in code instead of rediscovered by the LLM every time, 143 (3) computed ratios and changes that are verifiable, and (4) clear, testable error messages. 144 **[DECIDE]** Add a guarded `run_sql` fallback (read-only connection, `SELECT` only, row limit) for questions the tools don't cover? 145 *Proposal: no for the MVP. It weakens the guarantees and the tools cover the brief's examples.* 146 147 Yeah we can add run_sql for flexibility. 148 149 ### 3.5 Tool errors are messages, not crashes 150 ```json 151 {"error": "unknown_area", "message": "No area matches 'Westeros'.", "hint": "Use find_areas first. Valid region codes: AFE, AFW, EAP, ECA, LCR, MENAAP, SAR"} 152 ``` 153 154 155 The model sees the error and can recover (call `find_areas`, then retry). Errors count toward the tool budget. 156 157 --- 158 159 ## 4. Verification: Proof-Carrying Numbers (adapted from World Bank DECDG) 160 161 ```mermaid 162 flowchart LR 163 R[Tool row] -->|claim_id = hash of source, ind, area, org, dims, snapshot, field| REG[(Claim registry
per conversation)] 164 A[final_answer text] --> P[Parse claim tags] 165 P --> C{Compare shown value
vs source value} 166 REG --> C 167 C -->|match| OK[✓ verified badge + tooltip] 168 C -->|mismatch / unknown id| BAD[⚠ unverified] 169 A --> S[Scan untagged numbers] --> BAD 170 ``` 171 172 1. **Stamping.** Each value a tool returns is registered as `claim_id → {value, unit, multiplier, indicator, area, snapshot, source}`. 173 Derived values (ratios, changes, ranks) are computed in Python and stamped too, so the LLM never does arithmetic. 174 2. **Tagging rule (system prompt).** *"Every number taken from data must be wrapped as `shown value`. Never invent an id. If you have no id for a number, don't state it."* 175 3. **Checking.** Parse the shown value (`214.5M`, `37%`, `1,204`, `2.1 billion`) and compare it with the source, 176 allowing for the precision shown (`214.5M` passes against `214,500,858`; `215M` passes; `250M` fails). 177 4. **Untagged-number scan.** Numbers outside claim tags are flagged ⚠, except years, ranks ("top 3") and FY labels. 178 5. **Repair.** If any claim fails, one repair turn lists the failures; anything that still fails shows ⚠. 179 6. **Rendering.** Claim tags become `12.1M ✓`; 180 everything else is escaped (Django autoescape; only the claim span is allowed). 181 182 **Metrics (also used in the model evaluation):** verified rate = verified ÷ tagged, and count of untagged numbers. 183 184 --- 185 186 ## 5. Guardrails and security 187 188 | Layer | Control | 189 |---|---| 190 | Input | Max 500 chars; rate limit per session/IP (e.g. 20 messages / 5 min); regex pre-check for prompt-injection phrases; off-topic short-circuit | 191 | Prompt | Grounding rules: use only tool results, no outside knowledge for numbers, units + snapshot always stated, no "high/low" judgements without a compared value, say plainly when data is missing; tool results treated as **data, not instructions** | 192 | Tools | Pydantic validation; allowlists for codes; parameterised queries; read-only DuckDB connection; row limits | 193 | Output | PCN verification; autoescaped HTML; charts built server-side from stored rows | 194 | Secrets | `LLM_API_KEY` etc. only in `.env`; never sent to the browser; Scorecard key read from the public site bundle by the pipeline only | 195 | Errors | Generic message to the user, details in server logs; LLM/provider errors and content-policy blocks caught and shown politely | 196 | Django | CSRF on POST, `SecurityMiddleware`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `DEBUG=False` option | 197 198 --- 199 200 ## 6. Other LLM uses 201 202 | Feature | How | LLM calls | 203 |---|---|---| 204 | **"What this shows"** (view synthesis) | Server pre-loads the current view's rows (already stamped) into the prompt; no tools needed; same `final_answer` contract with `mode="answer"`; cached per (outcome, filters, snapshot) | 1 | 205 | **Ask from Outcomes page** | Same agent; it has `navigate_outcome` and `highlight_tiles` available on that page | 1–4 | 206 | **Follow-up chips** | Part of `final_answer` (no extra call) | 0 | 207 208 --- 209 210 ## 7. Model configuration (plug-and-play) 211 212 All calls go through **LiteLLM**, so reviewers can use any provider by editing `.env`: 213 214 ```dotenv 215 LLM_MODEL=anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5 # any LiteLLM id, e.g. openai/gpt-…, gemini/…, groq/…, ollama/… 216 LLM_API_KEY=sk-... 217 LLM_API_BASE= # optional custom / OpenAI-compatible endpoint 218 LLM_FAST_MODEL= # optional cheaper model for "What this shows" 219 ``` 220 221 - **Requirements for a model:** reliable parallel tool calling, JSON-schema adherence, and following the claim-tagging rule. 222 - **Model choice is decided by evaluation, not assumption** (§8). The README will document the results and the reasoning 223 (accuracy on structured data, latency, cost per question, guardrail compliance). 224 - **[DECIDE]** Which provider/key will we test with? It affects which candidates we can benchmark. 225 226 I can provide anthropic keys for testing abd building. 227 228 --- 229 230 ## 8. Evaluation (for the model choice) 231 232 - **Golden set:** ~15 questions with known answers computed directly from DuckDB. They cover filters ("girls in Ghana"), 233 single facts, comparisons, rankings, snapshot change, definitions, a no-data case and 2 out-of-scope prompts, 234 including the brief's three example questions. 235 236 237 - **Per model:** correct mode/tools · answer correctness (numbers match) · **PCN verified rate** · untagged numbers · 238 correct refusals · median latency · tokens → cost per question. 239 - `python manage.py run_evals --models a,b,c` → results table in the README. 240 241 242 243 --- 244 245 ## 9. Django layout 246 247 ``` 248 q1_prototype/ 249 manage.py 250 scorecard_explorer/ settings.py (reads .env), urls.py 251 explorer/ 252 views.py Outcomes page, Explorer page, HTMX partials (charts, chips, cards) 253 queries.py typed read-only DuckDB query service (used by views AND tools) 254 templates/ static/ HTMX + Plotly.js, one CSS theme 255 assistant/ 256 agent.py loop: LiteLLM tool calling, budgets, repair, SSE events 257 tools.py tool schemas (pydantic) + implementations → queries.py 258 prompts.py system prompt, grounding + claim rules 259 pcn.py claim registry, parser, verifier, renderer 260 guards.py input checks, rate limit 261 evals/ golden questions + runner (management command) 262 pipeline/ shared with Q3: fetch_scorecard.py, fetch_data360.py, clean.py, build_db.py 263 data/ raw/ (API extracts) + scorecard.duckdb 264 ``` 265 266 **Streaming:** `/api/chat` returns a Django `StreamingHttpResponse` (`text/event-stream`) with events 267 `status` → `ui_action` → `answer` → `done`. The browser uses a small `fetch` stream reader. 268 Conversation history and the claim registry are kept in the Django session (server-side), keyed per Explorer tab. 269 270 --- 271 272 ## 10. Open decisions 273 1. One agent with view tools (B) vs router + pipelines (A) → *proposal: B* 274 2. Guarded `run_sql` fallback → *proposal: not in the MVP* 275 3. LLM provider/key for testing and evaluation < I will provide you with some> 276 4. Max tool calls 6 / history 6 turns: OK? 277

How a message is answered: the agent loop ### 2.1 Design choice: one agent with two kinds of tools | Option | How it works | Trade-off | |---|---|---| | A. Router → separate pipelines (as in the WB chatbot) | A cheap classifier picks filter / analyze / explain / clarify, then a dedicated chain runs | More predictable, but more code and an extra LLM call per message | | **B. One tool-calling agent (proposed)** | One agent with **data tools** (read) and **view tools** (change the canvas). The model decides: "girls in Ghana" → `apply_filters`; "compare…" → data tools → answer | Less code, naturally handles mixed requests ("show Ghana and compare it to Kenya"), still bounded by the tool budget | **[DECIDE]** Proposal: **A**, with a deterministic pre-check (§5) handling empty, overly long and obviously off-topic input before any LLM call. ### 2.2 The loop ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor U as User participant API as /api/chat (Django, SSE) participant G as Input guard participant A as Agent (LiteLLM) participant T as Tools participant V as Verifier U->>API: message + view state {outcome, filters, snapshot} API->>G: length, rate limit, injection patterns G-->>API: ok API->>A: system prompt + view state + history (last 6 turns) + tool schemas loop max 6 tool calls A->>T: tool call (JSON args) T->>T: validate args (pydantic + allowlists) T-->>A: rows + claim_ids (or structured error) API-->>U: SSE status: "Querying electricity results for AFW…" end A->>API: final_answer(card, narrative with tags, chart refs, follow-ups) API->>V: verify every claim tag + scan for untagged numbers alt any claim fails V->>A: repair once: "claims c_9f2 and c_771 don't match the source, please fix" A->>API: revised final_answer end API-->>U: SSE: ui_actions, answer (HTML with ✓/⚠), done ``` **Response contract.** The agent must finish by calling `final_answer`, so every response has the same structure: ```json { "mode": "filters | answer | explain | clarify | out_of_scope", "headline": {"label": "People provided with electricity, AFW (FY25)", "value_html": "12.1M"}, "narrative_md": "Western & Central Africa has reached 12.1M people …", "charts": [{"type": "bar", "from_result": "r2", "x": "area", "y": ["achieved", "expected"]}], "follow_ups": ["Which countries drive the gap in AFW?", "Show this for women only"], "sources": ["r1", "r2"], "clarify_options": [] } ``` - **Charts reference tool results (`from_result`), not numbers.** The server builds the Plotly spec from the stored rows, so the LLM can't put a wrong number into a chart. - **View actions** (`apply_filters`, `highlight_tiles`) are tool calls during the loop, so a filter-only request costs one round-trip: `apply_filters` → `final_answer(mode="filters", narrative="Showing Ghana, women…")`. ### 2.3 Budgets and settings | Setting | Value | Why | |---|---|---| | Max tool calls per message | 6 | Covers multi-step comparisons while keeping cost and latency bounded | | Temperature | 0 | Reproducible; analysis, not creative writing | | History sent | last 6 turns + current view state | Follow-ups ("and for youth?") work without long contexts | | Timeout | 30 s total, 10 s per LLM call | Generic error with a retry button after that | | Repair attempts | 1 | One chance to fix failed claims; then show ⚠ honestly | --- ## 3. Tools All tools are **read-only**, **typed** (pydantic schemas, exported as JSON Schema for function calling) and **allowlisted** (indicator codes, area codes, dimension values are validated against the database before any query runs). Every data row returned carries a `claim_id`. Every tool result gets a `result_id` (`r1`, `r2`, …) for charts and sources. ### 3.1 Discovery tools | Tool | Arguments | Returns | Example use | |---|---|---|---| | `search_indicators` | `query`, `outcome_area?`, `type? (results/context/vision)` | matching indicators: code, name, unit, outcome area, available dimensions | "digital access" → `CSC_RES_BRO_INTE`, `CSC_RES_DIG_ENA_SERV`, `IT_NET_USER_ZS` | | `find_areas` | `query` (free text, e.g. "western africa", "fragile states", "Ghana") | resolved codes: `{type: REGION, code: AFW}`, `{type: COUNTRY, code: GH}`, `{type: FCS}` | entity resolution with fuzzy matching on names and aliases | | `get_definition` | `ind_code` | definition, unit, notes, source (metadata) | "what does 'expected' mean?" | ### 3.2 Data tools | Tool | Arguments | Returns | |---|---|---| | `get_results` | `ind_code`, `areas[]`, `org=WBG`, `sex/age/disability=_T`, `snapshot=FY25` | achieved, expected, **delivery ratio (computed in code)**, unit, snapshot date, per area | | `rank_areas` | `ind_code`, `area_type (REGION/COUNTRY)`, `metric (achieved/expected/ratio/gap)`, `order`, `top_n≤15`, dims | ranked rows + rank | | `outcome_overview` | `outcome_area? (or all)`, `areas[]=[ACW]`, `snapshot` | all Results indicators in scope with achieved/expected/ratio, for "biggest gaps" or "top lagging" | | `compare_snapshots` | `ind_code`, `area`, `snapshots[]` | values per FY + **change computed in code** (absolute and %) | | `get_context_series` | `ind_code`, `areas[]`, `year_from?`, `year_to?` | Client Context / Vision time series + latest value + change | | `get_wdi_context` | `indicator ∈ {population, gdp_per_capita, poverty_300, electricity_access, internet_users}`, `areas[]`, `year?` | Data360 values (from the pipeline cache), with source | ### 3.3 View tools (change the canvas; no data returned) | Tool | Arguments | Effect | |---|---|---| | `apply_filters` | any of `region, country, income, group, org, sex, age, disability, snapshot` (validated) | updates filter state; the canvas re-renders through HTMX | | `navigate_outcome` | `outcome_slug`, `filters?` | from the Outcomes page: open the Explorer with filters already set | | `highlight_tiles` | `outcome_slugs[]` | highlight tiles named in a cross-area answer | ### 3.4 Final tool `final_answer`: the response contract above (§2.2). It weakens the guarantees and the tools cover the brief's examples.* Yeah we can add run_sql for flexibility. ### 3.5 Tool errors are messages, not crashes ```json {"error": "unknown_area", "message": "No area matches 'Westeros'.", "hint": "Use find_areas first. Verification: Proof-Carrying Numbers (adapted from World Bank DECDG) ```mermaid flowchart LR R[Tool row] -->|claim_id = hash of source, ind, area, org, dims, snapshot, field| REG[(Claim registry
per conversation)] A[final_answer text] --> P[Parse claim tags] P --> C{Compare shown value
vs source value} REG --> C C -->|match| OK[✓ verified badge + tooltip] C -->|mismatch / unknown id| BAD[⚠ unverified] A --> S[Scan untagged numbers] --> BAD ``` 1. **Stamping.** Each value a tool returns is registered as `claim_id → {value, unit, multiplier, indicator, area, snapshot, source}`. Derived values (ratios, changes, ranks) are computed in Python and stamped too, so the LLM never does arithmetic. 2. **Tagging rule (system prompt).** *"Every number taken from data must be wrapped as `shown value`. Never invent an id. If you have no id for a number, don't state it."* 3. **Checking.** Parse the shown value (`214.5M`, `37%`, `1,204`, `2.1 billion`) and compare it with the source, allowing for the precision shown (`214.5M` passes against `214,500,858`; `215M` passes; `250M` fails). 4. **Untagged-number scan.** Numbers outside claim tags are flagged ⚠, except years, ranks ("top 3") and FY labels. 5. **Repair.** If any claim fails, one repair turn lists the failures; anything that still fails shows ⚠. 6. **Rendering.** Claim tags become `12.1M ✓`; everything else is escaped (Django autoescape; only the claim span is allowed). **Metrics (also used in the model evaluation):** verified rate = verified ÷ tagged, and count of untagged numbers. --- ## 5. Guardrails and security | Layer | Control | |---|---| | Input | Max 500 chars; rate limit per session/IP (e.g. 20 messages / 5 min); regex pre-check for prompt-injection phrases; off-topic short-circuit | | Prompt | Grounding rules: use only tool results, no outside knowledge for numbers, units + snapshot always stated, no "high/low" judgements without a compared value, say plainly when data is missing; tool results treated as **data, not instructions** | | Tools | Pydantic validation; allowlists for codes; parameterised queries; read-only DuckDB connection; row limits | | Output | PCN verification; autoescaped HTML; charts built server-side from stored rows | | Secrets | `LLM_API_KEY` etc. only in `.env`; never sent to the browser; Scorecard key read from the public site bundle by the pipeline only | | Errors | Generic message to the user, details in server logs; LLM/provider errors and content-policy blocks caught and shown politely | | Django | CSRF on POST, `SecurityMiddleware`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `DEBUG=False` option | --- ## 6. Other LLM uses | Feature | How | LLM calls | |---|---|---| | **"What this shows"** (view synthesis) | Server pre-loads the current view's rows (already stamped) into the prompt; no tools needed; same `final_answer` contract with `mode="answer"`; cached per (outcome, filters, snapshot) | 1 | | **Ask from Outcomes page** | Same agent; it has `navigate_outcome` and `highlight_tiles` available on that page | 1–4 | | **Follow-up chips** | Part of `final_answer` (no extra call) | 0 | --- ## 7. Model configuration (plug-and-play) All calls go through **LiteLLM**, so reviewers can use any provider by editing `.env`: ```dotenv LLM_MODEL=anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5 # any LiteLLM id, e.g. openai/gpt-…, gemini/…, groq/…, ollama/… LLM_API_KEY=sk-... LLM_API_BASE= # optional custom / OpenAI-compatible endpoint LLM_FAST_MODEL= # optional cheaper model for "What this shows" ``` - **Requirements for a model:** reliable parallel tool calling, JSON-schema adherence, and following the claim-tagging rule. - **Model choice is decided by evaluation, not assumption** (§8). The README will document the results and the reasoning (accuracy on structured data, latency, cost per question, guardrail compliance). - **[DECIDE]** Which provider/key will we test with? It affects which candidates we can benchmark. I can provide anthropic keys for testing abd building. --- ## 8. Evaluation (for the model choice) - **Golden set:** ~15 questions with known answers computed directly from DuckDB. They cover filters ("girls in Ghana"), single facts, comparisons, rankings, snapshot change, definitions, a no-data case and 2 out-of-scope prompts, including the brief's three example questions. - **Per model:** correct mode/tools · answer correctness (numbers match) · **PCN verified rate** · untagged numbers · correct refusals · median latency · tokens → cost per question. - `python manage.py run_evals --models a,b,c` → results table in the README. --- ## 9. Django layout ``` q1_prototype/ manage.py scorecard_explorer/ settings.py (reads .env), urls.py explorer/ views.py Outcomes page, Explorer page, HTMX partials (charts, chips, cards) queries.py typed read-only DuckDB query service (used by views AND tools) templates/ static/ HTMX + Plotly.js, one CSS theme assistant/ agent.py loop: LiteLLM tool calling, budgets, repair, SSE events tools.py tool schemas (pydantic) + implementations → queries.py prompts.py system prompt, grounding + claim rules pcn.py claim registry, parser, verifier, renderer guards.py input checks, rate limit evals/ golden questions + runner (management command) pipeline/ shared with Q3: fetch_scorecard.py, fetch_data360.py, clean.py, build_db.py data/ raw/ (API extracts) + scorecard.duckdb ``` **Streaming:** `/api/chat` returns a Django `StreamingHttpResponse` (`text/event-stream`) with events `status` → `ui_action` → `answer` → `done`. The browser uses a small `fetch` stream reader. Conversation history and the claim registry are kept in the Django session (server-side), keyed per Explorer tab. --- ## 10. Open decisions 1. One agent with view tools (B) vs router + pipelines (A) → *proposal: B* 2. Guarded `run_sql` fallback → *proposal: not in the MVP* 3. LLM provider/key for testing and evaluation < I will provide you with some> 4. Max tool calls 6 / history 6 turns: OK?

ext.api.worldbank.org] --> P[fetch → parse → clean → tidy] D360[Data360 API
allowlisted WDI] --> P P --> DB[(DuckDB
scorecard.duckdb)] end subgraph App["Django app (q1_prototype/)"] V[Views + templates

filter · explain · analyze · clarify · out-of-scope] PL -->|tool calls| T[Tool registry
typed tools + guarded run_sql] T --> Q PL --> VER[Verifier
Proof-Carrying Numbers] Q --> DB end RT <-->|LiteLLM| LLMf[(Fast model)] PL <-->|LiteLLM| LLMm[(Main model)] B[Browser

How a message is answered: router + pipelines **Why router + pipelines:** each kind of request follows a **fixed, testable path**, so behaviour is predictable and robust. The World Bank's data-ai-chatbot uses the same pattern. The cost is one extra (small, fast) LLM call per message. Simple filter requests then need **no further LLM call**, so they end up faster than with a single agent. ### 2.1 Overview ```mermaid flowchart TD M[User message + view state] --> G{Input guard
deterministic} G -->|blocked| X[Polite message] G --> R[Router
fast model · temp 0 · JSON schema] R --> ER[Entity resolver
deterministic: names → codes] ER -->|intent = filter| F[Filter pipeline] ER -->|intent = explain| E[Explain pipeline] ER -->|intent = analyze| A[Analyze pipeline] ER -->|intent = clarify| C[Clarify pipeline] ER -->|intent = out_of_scope| O[Out-of-scope pipeline] F --> UI[ui_actions: chips + canvas] A --> VER[Verifier ✓/⚠] --> ANS[Answer card + chart + narrative + follow-ups] E --> ANS C --> OPT[Clarifying question + option chips] O --> SUG[Redirect + suggested questions] ``` ### 2.2 Router (1 fast LLM call) Input: the message, the view state `{page, outcome, filters, snapshot}`, and a summary of the conversation so far. Output (strict JSON schema, temperature 0): ```json { "intent": "filter | explain | analyze | clarify | out_of_scope", "also_apply_filters": true, "entities": { "areas": ["western africa"], "countries": [], "groups": [], "income": [], "org": null, "sex": "F", "age": null, "disability": null, "snapshot": null, "outcome_hint": "energy", "indicator_hint": "electricity access" }, "missing": [], "reason": "user narrows the view to women in AFW" } ``` - **Mixed requests** ("show Ghana and compare it to Kenya"): `intent=analyze` + `also_apply_filters=true`, so the canvas updates *and* the analysis runs. - **The router only extracts text; it never produces codes.** The **entity resolver** (plain Python, fuzzy matching against the database's names and aliases) turns "western africa" into `REGION:AFW` and "Ghana" into `COUNTRY:GH`. That step is deterministic and testable. ext.api.worldbank.org] --> P[fetch → parse → clean → tidy] D360[Data360 API
allowlisted WDI] --> P P --> DB[(DuckDB
scorecard.duckdb)] end subgraph App["Django app (q1_prototype/)"] V[Views + templates
Outcomes · Explorer] --> Q[Query service
typed, read-only] CH[/api/chat SSE/] --> RT[Router] RT --> PL[Pipelines
filter · explain · analyze · clarify · out-of-scope] PL -->|tool calls| T[Tool registry
typed tools + guarded run_sql] T --> Q PL --> VER[Verifier
Proof-Carrying Numbers] Q --> DB end RT <-->|LiteLLM| LLMf[(Fast model)] PL <-->|LiteLLM| LLMm[(Main model)] B[Browser
HTMX + Plotly.js] <--> V B <-->|SSE events| CH ``` - **Data is never fetched live while a user waits.** The pipeline builds `scorecard.duckdb` ahead of time; the app only reads it. - **The LLM never writes to anything.** It reads through typed tools or a guarded, read-only `run_sql` (§3.4). --- ## 2. How a message is answered: router + pipelines **Why router + pipelines:** each kind of request follows a **fixed, testable path**, so behaviour is predictable and robust. The World Bank's data-ai-chatbot uses the same pattern. The cost is one extra (small, fast) LLM call per message. Simple filter requests then need **no further LLM call**, so they end up faster than with a single agent. ### 2.1 Overview ```mermaid flowchart TD M[User message + view state] --> G{Input guard
deterministic} G -->|blocked| X[Polite message] G --> R[Router
fast model · temp 0 · JSON schema] R --> ER[Entity resolver
deterministic: names → codes] ER -->|intent = filter| F[Filter pipeline] ER -->|intent = explain| E[Explain pipeline] ER -->|intent = analyze| A[Analyze pipeline] ER -->|intent = clarify| C[Clarify pipeline] ER -->|intent = out_of_scope| O[Out-of-scope pipeline] F --> UI[ui_actions: chips + canvas] A --> VER[Verifier ✓/⚠] --> ANS[Answer card + chart + narrative + follow-ups] E --> ANS C --> OPT[Clarifying question + option chips] O --> SUG[Redirect + suggested questions] ``` ### 2.2 Router (1 fast LLM call) Input: the message, the view state `{page, outcome, filters, snapshot}`, and a summary of the conversation so far. That step is deterministic and testable. Unresolvable entities → `clarify`. - Rules: a missing year is never a reason to clarify (default = latest snapshot); a missing outcome on an outcome page = the current one. ### 2.3 Pipelines | Pipeline | Steps | LLM calls | Typical latency | |---|---|---|---| | **filter** | resolve → validate against allowlists → update filter state → templated confirmation ("Showing women in Western & Central Africa. [undo]") | 0 (after router) | < 1 s | | **explain** | look up indicator/term metadata → main model writes a short explanation **from the metadata only** | 1 | ~2 s | | **analyze** | **research step** (tool loop) → **writer step** (narrative with claim tags) → **verifier** (+1 repair) | 2–3 + tools | ~5–12 s | | **clarify** | templated question + option chips built from `missing` and the resolver's candidates | 0 | < 1 s | | **out_of_scope** | templated redirect + 3 suggested questions for the current outcome | 0 | < 1 s | ### 2.4 The analyze pipeline (research → write → verify) Following the World Bank chatbot, **retrieving data and writing the answer are separate steps**: ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant API as /api/chat (SSE) participant RS as Research step (main model) participant T as Tools participant W as Writer step (main model) participant V as Verifier API->>RS: question + resolved entities + view state + tool schemas loop max 6 tool calls RS->>T: typed tool or run_sql T-->>RS: rows stamped with claim_ids (or structured error + hint) API-->>API: SSE status: "Ranking regions by delivery…" end RS-->>API: research packet (which results answer what; no numbers rewritten) API->>W: RAW tool results (verbatim JSON, in system message) + packet + writing rules W-->>API: final_answer {headline, narrative with tags, charts→result_ids, follow-ups, sources} API->>V: verify claims + scan untagged numbers alt failures V->>W: one repair turn listing failed claims W-->>API: revised final_answer end API-->>API: SSE: ui_actions, answer (✓/⚠ HTML), done ``` - **Research step:** decides *which* data is needed and calls tools. It's told not to write numbers, only to explain which results answer the question. - **Writer step:** sees the raw tool output directly, so numbers are copied from the source, not paraphrased through another LLM pass. - **Response contract** (`final_answer`, the same for every pipeline that writes text): ```json { "mode": "answer | explain", "headline": {"label": "People provided with electricity, AFW (FY25)", "value_html": "12.1M"}, "narrative_md": "Western & Central Africa has reached 12.1M people …", "charts": [{"type": "bar", "from_result": "r2", "x": "area", "y": ["achieved", "expected"]}], "follow_ups": ["Which countries drive the gap in AFW?", "Show this for women only"], "sources": ["r1", "r2"] } ``` Charts reference tool results (`from_result`); the server builds the Plotly spec from stored rows, so charts can't contain invented numbers. ### 2.5 Conversation memory: as long as the user wants - The **full conversation** is stored server-side (Django session/DB) with no turn limit. - What's **sent to the model** is bounded so cost and latency stay flat in long chats: the **last 8 turns verbatim** plus a **rolling summary** of earlier turns (refreshed by the fast model when the history grows past the window), plus the current view state. - The **claim registry persists for the whole conversation**, so numbers from earlier answers stay verifiable when referred to again. ### 2.6 Budgets and settings | Setting | Value | Why | |---|---|---| | Max tool calls (research step) | 6 | Keeps the wait short (shown live as status messages) | | Repair attempts | 1 | One chance to fix failed claims, then show ⚠ honestly | | Temperature | 0 (router, research), 0.2 (writer) | Deterministic routing and data access; slightly more natural prose | | Conversation | unlimited; model context = last 8 turns + rolling summary | §2.5 | | Timeouts | 10 s per LLM call, 45 s per message | After that: partial answer or a generic error with retry | --- ## 3. Tools All tools are **read-only** and **typed** (pydantic schemas, exported as JSON Schema). Codes are validated against the database before any query runs. Every data row returned carries a `claim_id`, and every tool result has a `result_id` (`r1`, `r2`, …). The research step should **prefer typed tools** and use `run_sql` only when no typed tool fits. ### 3.1 Discovery tools | Tool | Arguments | Returns | |---|---|---| | `search_indicators` | `query`, `outcome_area?`, `type? (results/context/vision)` | code, name, unit, outcome area, available dimensions | | `get_definition` | `ind_code` | definition, unit, notes, source | | `describe_schema` | — | tables, columns and meanings available to `run_sql` | *(Area names are resolved by the deterministic entity resolver before the pipeline starts; `find_areas` stays available as a tool for multi-step cases.)* ### 3.2 Data tools | Tool | Arguments | Returns | |---|---|---| | `get_results` | `ind_code`, `areas[]`, `org=WBG`, `sex/age/disability=_T`, `snapshot=FY25` | achieved, expected, **delivery ratio (computed in code)**, unit, snapshot date, per area | | `rank_areas` | `ind_code`, `area_type (REGION/COUNTRY)`, `metric (achieved/expected/ratio/gap)`, `order`, `top_n≤15`, dims | ranked rows + rank | | `outcome_overview` | `outcome_area? (or all)`, `areas[]=[ACW]`, `snapshot` | all Results indicators in scope, with achieved/expected/ratio | | `compare_snapshots` | `ind_code`, `area`, `snapshots[]` | values per FY + **change computed in code** | | `get_context_series` | `ind_code`, `areas[]`, `year_from?`, `year_to?` | Client Context / Vision time series + latest value + change | | `get_wdi_context` | `indicator ∈ allowlist`, `areas[]`, `year?` | Data360 values (pipeline cache), with source | ### 3.3 View actions `apply_filters`, `navigate_outcome`, `highlight_tiles`. These are triggered by the **filter pipeline** (and by `also_apply_filters`), not chosen freely by the model. ### 3.4 `run_sql`: flexible, but guarded For questions the typed tools don't cover (e.g. "which outcome areas have the largest gap for youth relative to women?"). | Guard | Implementation | |---|---| | Read-only | DuckDB opened with `read_only=True`; `enable_external_access=false` (no files, URLs, extensions) | | One SELECT only | Parsed with `sqlglot`: single `SELECT`/`WITH` statement; no DDL/DML, `ATTACH`, `COPY`, `PRAGMA`, `SET`, table functions | | Allowlisted objects | Only curated analysis **views** (e.g. `v_results`, `v_context`, `v_areas`, `v_indicators`), not raw tables | | Bounded | `LIMIT 200` added if missing; 5 s timeout; result size cap | | Verifiable | Every returned cell is stamped with a `claim_id`, so `run_sql` numbers get ✓ like any other tool | | Transparent | The SQL is shown in "How I got this" | | Recoverable | SQL errors return the message + `describe_schema` hint; counted in the tool budget | ### 3.5 Tool errors are messages, not crashes ```json {"error": "unknown_area", "message": "No area matches 'Westeros'.", "hint": "Valid region codes: AFE, AFW, EAP, ECA, LCR, MENAAP, SAR"} ``` The model sees the error and can recover. Errors count toward the tool budget. --- ## 4. Verification: Proof-Carrying Numbers (adapted from World Bank DECDG) ```mermaid flowchart LR R[Tool row / SQL cell] -->|claim_id = hash of source, ind, area, org, dims, snapshot, field| REG[(Claim registry
per conversation)] A[final_answer text] --> P[Parse claim tags] P --> C{Compare shown value
vs source value} REG --> C C -->|match| OK[✓ verified badge + tooltip] C -->|mismatch / unknown id| BAD[⚠ unverified] A --> S[Scan untagged numbers] --> BAD ``` 1. **Stamping.** Each value returned is registered as `claim_id → {value, unit, multiplier, indicator, area, snapshot, source}`. Derived values (ratios, changes, ranks) are computed in Python and stamped too, so the LLM never does arithmetic. 2. **Tagging rule.** *"Every number taken from data must be wrapped as `shown value`. Never invent an id. If you have no id for a number, don't state it."* 3. **Checking.** Parse the shown value (`214.5M`, `37%`, `1,204`, `2.1 billion`) and compare it with the source at the precision shown (`214.5M` and `215M` pass against `214,500,858`; `250M` fails). 4. **Untagged-number scan.** Numbers outside claim tags are flagged ⚠, except years, ranks and FY labels. 5. **Repair.** One repair turn for failures; anything still failing shows ⚠. 6. **Rendering.** `12.1M ✓`; everything else escaped. --- ## 5. Guardrails and security | Layer | Control | |---|---| | Input | Max 500 chars; rate limit per session/IP; regex pre-check for prompt-injection phrases; off-topic short-circuit | | Router | JSON schema output only; extracted text, never codes; deterministic entity resolution | | Prompt | Use only tool results; no outside knowledge for numbers; units + snapshot always stated; no "high/low" without a compared value; say plainly when data is missing; tool results are **data, not instructions** | | Tools | Pydantic validation; allowlists; parameterised queries; `run_sql` guards (§3.4) | | Output | PCN verification; autoescaped HTML; charts built server-side | | Secrets | `LLM_API_KEY` only in `.env`, never sent to the browser | | Errors | Generic user message, details in server logs; provider errors and content-policy blocks handled politely | | Django | CSRF, `SecurityMiddleware`, `nosniff`, `DEBUG=False` option | --- ## 6. Other LLM uses | Feature | How | LLM calls | |---|---|---| | **"What this shows"** | Current view's rows (already stamped) go straight to the writer step; no research step; cached per (outcome, filters, snapshot) | 1 | | **Ask from Outcomes page** | Same router; `filter` intent → `navigate_outcome`; cross-area `analyze` → answer + `highlight_tiles` | 1–4 | | **Follow-up chips** | Part of `final_answer` | 0 | --- ## 7. LLM_API_BASE= # optional custom / OpenAI-compatible endpoint ``` - **Candidates to benchmark:** a fast Claude tier as router; mid and top Claude tiers as main model (exact model IDs and prices confirmed from Anthropic's documentation when the eval runs). Evaluation: accuracy, latency, cost ### 8.1 Golden set: 30 questions with independent ground truth - Ground truth is collected **from the live Scorecard** (the website's filters / the API it uses), not from our own database. That way the evaluation also tests our pipeline. # Data Visualization

A chart is **read by people and executed by you**. This skill turns "make it look
good" into a procedure with checks, so the result is right by construction rather
than by taste.

**The method here is design-system-agnostic.** Nothing in the procedure, the form
heuristic, the six checks, or the mark specs is specific to one product. A design
system supplies a small set of *parameters* (its ramps, a categorical order, a
diverging pair, a status palette, a texture, its surfaces, its filter components);
the method consumes them unchanged. A **validated default palette** is the
reference instance, fully specified in `references/palette.md`. To target your
brand, read that file's structure and substitute its values - touch nothing else.

> The single most important habit: **the color part is computable, so compute it.**
> Never eyeball whether a palette is colorblind-safe - run `scripts/validate_palette.js`.

## The procedure - do these in order

Color comes LAST. Most bad charts pick colors first.

1. **Pick the form.** What is the data's job - magnitude, identity, polarity, a
   single headline, change-over-time? The job picks the chart type, and sometimes
   the answer is *not a chart* (a stat tile or hero number). -> `references/choosing-a-form.md`
2. **Assign color by the job it does.** Categorical (identity), sequential
   (magnitude), diverging (polarity), or status (state) - each has one rule.
   Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled. -> `references/color-formula.md`
3. **VALIDATE the palette - run the script, don't reason about Delta E.**
   `node scripts/validate_palette.js "<hex,hex,...>" --mode light` (relative to
   this skill's base directory - or load it as `<script type="module">` in the
   chart's own page, where it reads
   `data-palette` off `<body>` and logs a `console.table` report). It returns
   pass/fail on the lightness band, chroma floor, adjacent-pair CVD separation,
   the normal-vision floor, and contrast. Fix anything that FAILs before continuing. Re-run for
   `--mode dark` with that mode's surface.
4. **Apply mark specs & spacers.** Thin marks, 4px rounded data-ends anchored to
   the baseline, 2px lines, >=8px markers, a 2px surface gap between fills (stacked
   segments and adjacent bars alike) and a 2px surface ring on overlapping marks,
   selective direct labels. -> `references/marks-and-anatomy.md`
5. **Add the hover layer - by default.** An HTML/SVG chart *is* interactive; ship
   a crosshair+tooltip on line/area and a per-mark hover tooltip on bar/dot/cell.
   The only form that skips it is a bare stat tile with no plot. Hit targets bigger
   than the mark; filters in one row above the charts. -> `references/interaction.md`
6. **Final accessibility pass.** For >= 2 series a legend is always present and <= 4
   are also direct-labeled (a single series needs no legend box - the title names
   it), so identity is never color-alone; a table view exists; dark mode is **selected** - its own
   steps from the same ramps, validated against the dark surface, not an automatic
   flip; texture is available for the CVD/print/forced-colors case.
7. **Render it and look at it.** The validator checks color, not layout - open or
   screenshot the output and eyeball it for label collisions, geometry, and overflow
   before calling it done.

Then check the result against **`references/anti-patterns.md`** - it is the catalog
of what goes wrong. If your chart matches an entry, it's wrong.

## Non-negotiables (true in every design system)

- **Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled.** A 9th series is never a
  generated hue - it folds into "Other," small multiples, or composite encoding.
- **One axis.** Never a dual-axis chart (two y-scales). Two measures of different
  scale -> two charts, small multiples, or indexed to a common base. *(This is the
  #1 chart mistake - see anti-patterns.)*
- **Color follows the entity, never its rank.** A filter that changes the series
  count must not repaint the survivors.
- **Sequential = one hue, light->dark. Diverging = two hues + a neutral gray
  midpoint.** Never a rainbow; never a hue at the diverging midpoint.
- **Run the validator before shipping any categorical palette.** CVD Delta E >= 8 is the
  target (OKLab ×100); 6-8 is a floor that is legal ONLY with secondary encoding. A
  normal-vision floor below 15 is a hard FAIL - full-color readers can't tell the
  pair apart; re-step it on the adjacent pairlist (secondary encoding does not excuse
  this one); under `--pairs all` cut series or facet instead - see check 4. A contrast WARN
  obligates visible labels or a table view - it is not dismissable.
- **Thin marks; a legend always present for >= 2 series (none for one), with
  selective direct labels (never a number on every point); recessive grid/axes.**
- **Text wears text tokens, never the series color** - values, labels, and legends
  stay in primary/secondary/muted ink; a colored mark beside them carries identity.
- **Status colors are reserved** (good/warning/serious/critical) and never reused
  for "series 4"; they ship with an icon + label, never color alone.

## Plugging in a design system

The method is invariant; only these parameters change per system. The reference
instance - every value filled in - is `references/palette.md`.

| Parameter | What the system provides |
|---|---|
| **Ramps** | the hue scales (named steps) the palette draws from |
| **Categorical theme** | the fixed hue order (a named theme); default + alternates |
| **Sequential hue** | the default single hue for magnitude |
| **Diverging pair** | two warm/cool poles + a neutral midpoint |
| **Status palette** | good / warning / serious / critical - steps distinct from categorical |
| **Texture fill** | one directional hand-drawn fill, used at 45° / 135° |
| **Surfaces** | light & dark chart-surface colors (the validator needs these) |
| **Filter controls** | date-range & dimension controls (behavioral spec in `interaction.md`) |

To onboard a new system: fill those rows, feed its ramps to the validator, and let
it snap each slot to the nearest passing step. Structure and rules stay as written.

## Reference files

| File | What it answers |
|------|-----------------|
| `references/choosing-a-form.md` | Which chart type / is it even a chart? |
| `references/color-formula.md` | The four jobs, the six checks, snap-to-passing |
| `references/marks-and-anatomy.md` | Mark specs, spacers, labels, figures, hero number |
| `references/interaction.md` | Tooltips & hover, filters & time ranges |
| `references/components.md` | The pieces a chart is made of - build each in plain HTML |
| `references/anti-patterns.md` | **What goes wrong - check every chart against this** |
| `references/palette.md` | **The reference palette instance** - every parameter, filled in; swap for your brand's |
| `scripts/validate_palette.js` | Runnable six-checks validator (run it; don't eyeball) |

# Data Visualization

A chart is **read by people and executed by you**. This skill turns "make it look
good" into a procedure with checks, so the result is right by construction rather
than by taste.

**The method here is design-system-agnostic.** Nothing in the procedure, the form
heuristic, the six checks, or the mark specs is specific to one product. A design
system supplies a small set of *parameters* (its ramps, a categorical order, a
diverging pair, a status palette, a texture, its surfaces, its filter components);
the method consumes them unchanged. A **validated default palette** is the
reference instance, fully specified in `references/palette.md`. To target your
brand, read that file's structure and substitute its values - touch nothing else.

> The single most important habit: **the color part is computable, so compute it.**
> Never eyeball whether a palette is colorblind-safe - run `scripts/validate_palette.js`.

## The procedure - do these in order

Color comes LAST. Most bad charts pick colors first.

1. **Pick the form.** What is the data's job - magnitude, identity, polarity, a
   single headline, change-over-time? The job picks the chart type, and sometimes
   the answer is *not a chart* (a stat tile or hero number). -> `references/choosing-a-form.md`
2. **Assign color by the job it does.** Categorical (identity), sequential
   (magnitude), diverging (polarity), or status (state) - each has one rule.
   Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled. -> `references/color-formula.md`
3. **VALIDATE the palette - run the script, don't reason about Delta E.**
   `node scripts/validate_palette.js "<hex,hex,...>" --mode light` (relative to
   this skill's base directory - or load it as `<script type="module">` in the
   chart's own page, where it reads
   `data-palette` off `<body>` and logs a `console.table` report). It returns
   pass/fail on the lightness band, chroma floor, adjacent-pair CVD separation,
   the normal-vision floor, and contrast. Fix anything that FAILs before continuing. Re-run for
   `--mode dark` with that mode's surface.
4. **Apply mark specs & spacers.** Thin marks, 4px rounded data-ends anchored to
   the baseline, 2px lines, >=8px markers, a 2px surface gap between fills (stacked
   segments and adjacent bars alike) and a 2px surface ring on overlapping marks,
   selective direct labels. -> `references/marks-and-anatomy.md`
5. **Add the hover layer - by default.** An HTML/SVG chart *is* interactive; ship
   a crosshair+tooltip on line/area and a per-mark hover tooltip on bar/dot/cell.
   The only form that skips it is a bare stat tile with no plot. Hit targets bigger
   than the mark; filters in one row above the charts. -> `references/interaction.md`
6. **Final accessibility pass.** For >= 2 series a legend is always present and <= 4
   are also direct-labeled (a single series needs no legend box - the title names
   it), so identity is never color-alone; a table view exists; dark mode is **selected** - its own
   steps from the same ramps, validated against the dark surface, not an automatic
   flip; texture is available for the CVD/print/forced-colors case.
7. **Render it and look at it.** The validator checks color, not layout - open or
   screenshot the output and eyeball it for label collisions, geometry, and overflow
   before calling it done.

Then check the result against **`references/anti-patterns.md`** - it is the catalog
of what goes wrong. If your chart matches an entry, it's wrong.

## Non-negotiables (true in every design system)

- **Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled.** A 9th series is never a
  generated hue - it folds into "Other," small multiples, or composite encoding.
- **One axis.** Never a dual-axis chart (two y-scales). Two measures of different
  scale -> two charts, small multiples, or indexed to a common base. *(This is the
  #1 chart mistake - see anti-patterns.)*
- **Color follows the entity, never its rank.** A filter that changes the series
  count must not repaint the survivors.
- **Sequential = one hue, light->dark. Diverging = two hues + a neutral gray
  midpoint.** Never a rainbow; never a hue at the diverging midpoint.
- **Run the validator before shipping any categorical palette.** CVD Delta E >= 8 is the
  target (OKLab ×100); 6-8 is a floor that is legal ONLY with secondary encoding. A
  normal-vision floor below 15 is a hard FAIL - full-color readers can't tell the
  pair apart; re-step it on the adjacent pairlist (secondary encoding does not excuse
  this one); under `--pairs all` cut series or facet instead - see check 4. A contrast WARN
  obligates visible labels or a table view - it is not dismissable.
- **Thin marks; a legend always present for >= 2 series (none for one), with
  selective direct labels (never a number on every point); recessive grid/axes.**
- **Text wears text tokens, never the series color** - values, labels, and legends
  stay in primary/secondary/muted ink; a colored mark beside them carries identity.
- **Status colors are reserved** (good/warning/serious/critical) and never reused
  for "series 4"; they ship with an icon + label, never color alone.

## Plugging in a design system

The method is invariant; only these parameters change per system. The reference
instance - every value filled in - is `references/palette.md`.

| Parameter | What the system provides |
|---|---|
| **Ramps** | the hue scales (named steps) the palette draws from |
| **Categorical theme** | the fixed hue order (a named theme); default + alternates |
| **Sequential hue** | the default single hue for magnitude |
| **Diverging pair** | two warm/cool poles + a neutral midpoint |
| **Status palette** | good / warning / serious / critical - steps distinct from categorical |
| **Texture fill** | one directional hand-drawn fill, used at 45° / 135° |
| **Surfaces** | light & dark chart-surface colors (the validator needs these) |
| **Filter controls** | date-range & dimension controls (behavioral spec in `interaction.md`) |

To onboard a new system: fill those rows, feed its ramps to the validator, and let
it snap each slot to the nearest passing step. Structure and rules stay as written.

## Reference files

| File | What it answers |
|------|-----------------|
| `references/choosing-a-form.md` | Which chart type / is it even a chart? |
| `references/color-formula.md` | The four jobs, the six checks, snap-to-passing |
| `references/marks-and-anatomy.md` | Mark specs, spacers, labels, figures, hero number |
| `references/interaction.md` | Tooltips & hover, filters & time ranges |
| `references/components.md` | The pieces a chart is made of - build each in plain HTML |
| `references/anti-patterns.md` | **What goes wrong - check every chart against this** |
| `references/palette.md` | **The reference palette instance** - every parameter, filled in; swap for your brand's |
| `scripts/validate_palette.js` | Runnable six-checks validator (run it; don't eyeball) |
